title: Untitled Submission: Dual Goal Network Planning Model for European Refugee Movement

source.pdf_page_offset_note: Physical page 1 is the summary sheet. Physical pages 2-20 are internally numbered 1-19, so the complete archived report has 20 pages.

context_sources.use: Official page 1 supports the first-time Problem F topic of Middle East-Europe refugee policy modeling, multidisciplinary methods, and a 20-page report; page 2 confirms control 43181 as an Outstanding Winner. The complete official statement is absent.

limitations: All 20 paper pages were rendered and reviewed through four contact sheets; formulas, route maps, static and dynamic flow tables, scaling table, letter, and references were checked visually.
Text extraction is complete but mathematical glyphs and punctuation contain mojibake; rendered pages control formula signs, factors, and table values.
The complete official 2016 Problem F statement is absent; only a press-release topic summary, general judging context, page limit, and official award listing are authoritative.

The paper prints no raw data, edge list, country-node mapping, PCA matrix or loadings, exact normalized objectives or weights, goal targets, solver details, code, monthly flow tables, scenario files, or machine-readable figures.
Several printed source and flow tables fail arithmetic and conservation checks, so transcription errors cannot be distinguished from solver-output errors without the missing reproduction bundle.

official_supported_requirements: Address policy modeling focused on Middle East-Europe refugee migration issues.
Use multidisciplinary skills such as mathematics, politics, government operations, data science, and analysis.
Use thorough data analysis, creative modeling, scientific methodology, effective writing, and visualization.
Communicate the result in a 20-page report.
paper_implied_tasks: Define crisis metrics for projected flows, route accessibility and safety, and receiving-country resources.
Create an optimal refugee-movement model with endogenous dynamics.
Recommend policies supporting safe and effective movement.
Test substantial exogenous events and model scalability.
Write a policy recommendation letter to senior migration decision makers.
task_reconstruction.paper_approach: Build a route impedance from time and death rate, use PCA for a destination living-quality score and a population fraction for capacity, reduce routes with Floyd-Warshall, solve weighted and goal-program allocations, add monthly service-dilution feedback and NGO scenarios, stress an edge cut and a capacity decline, expand arrivals tenfold, and address receiving states, NGOs, and the international community in a policy letter.
task_reconstruction.coverage_strengths: The submission visibly covers data, mathematics, endogenous dynamics, shocks, scale, policy, limitations, and executive communication within the confirmed 20-page limit.
task_reconstruction.coverage_gaps: Because the full statement is unavailable, exact official coverage is unprovable. The model omits law, consent, family and social networks, vulnerable groups, transit and asylum states, validated capacity, overflow recourse, reliable flow accounting, and evidence-based policy effects.

section_map.summary: Presents the metric-to-network-to-dynamic-to-policy-to-stress-test chain, main recommendations, and acknowledged scale limit.
Maps introduction, model, policy report, exogenous and scale extensions, conclusion, policy letter, and references.
Frames the 2015 European crisis, supplies paper-implied tasks, and removes social networks, language, policy conflict, and shocks from the base case.
Defines source distribution and a time-and-death route impedance with a uniform risk preference and mapped classes.
Defines five PCA indicators and a population-based maximum receiving ceiling.
Uses an unreported eleven-country Spearman analysis and maps major North Africa and Middle East routes into Europe.
Reduces the system to five source regions and eleven receiving countries and prints source, score, and ceiling tables.
Uses Floyd-Warshall and a constrained bi-objective flow skeleton, then prints a weighted objective with the living-quality direction reversed.
Shows the first flow map and an internally inconsistent table, then introduces lexicographic deviation minimization.
Shows the second flow map and inconsistent table and begins monthly endogenous destination feedback.
Defines monthly states and replaces the derived service-dilution coefficient with an unsupported value 300 times larger.
Adds an undefined social penalty, repeats the objective-sign defect, and iterates reallocation among European countries.

section_map.section: Dynamic Result, NGO Intervention, and Policy
section_map.summary: Calls a more even map closer to reality, assumes NGO effect sizes, and begins route-safety and reception-capacity policies.
Recommends rescue, frontline support, border coordination, Dublin reform, multicultural support, and host welfare, then defines exogenous events.
Discusses event mechanisms and removes the Hungary-Austria edge, reporting a change in an opaque mixed objective.
Assumes a 30-percent Belgian capacity loss and begins a larger-crisis test with inconsistent capacity definitions and negative values.
Admits allocation infeasibility, proposes NGO recourse qualitatively, and discusses delay, services, culture, and policy thresholds.
Lists route, ceiling, and country-power strengths and explicitly admits overflow, policy, culture, NGO, and international-organization gaps.
Groups concise recommendations for receiving countries, NGOs, and the international community.
Lists five sources on forced migration, statistics, and network protection but not the many operational datasets used.

contributions.summary: Connects measurement, graph optimization, feedback, shocks, scale, institutional policies, and a decision letter in a compact narrative.
Combines travel time and mortality into one route expression whose mechanism is visible even though it is uncalibrated.
Attempts to reduce food, health, welfare, and economic dimensions rather than using GDP alone.
Turns a visually complex migration geography into a small labeled graph suitable for explicit optimization.
Includes source balances and destination ceilings and recognizes opposing route and destination objectives.
Recognizes that arrivals alter local service conditions and therefore that one-shot allocation is structurally incomplete.
Addresses route rescue, frontline support, border coordination, institutional reform, host welfare, NGOs, and origin-region stabilization.
Uses an explicit edge deletion to show that policy and conflict can reconfigure the network.
Tests a tenfold crisis and does not hide that hard capacities make the allocation infeasible.
Names overflow, culture, policy, NGO, and international-governance omissions rather than claiming universal adequacy.
Uses actor headings and numbered actions to make recommendations easy for senior policy readers to scan.

nodes.label: Source flows, routes, deaths, time, country indicators, and population

broken_or_weak_handoffs: D1 to I2 lacks raw PCA data, scaling, loadings, orientation, and construct validation.
I2 to M1 reverses the stated living-quality objective and uses undisclosed normalization and weights.
M1 and M2 to reported results fail printed flow-conservation checks.
M2 to M3 replaces a derived coefficient and adds an undefined penalty without calibration.
S1 and S2 use arbitrary effects and incompatible capacity definitions.
P1 and L1 contain no quantified implementation, cost, legal, or uncertainty trace.

assumptions.summary: Removes family, friend, and information-network effects from route and destination decisions.
Assumes language differences have little effect even though integration and cultural conflict later motivate policy.
Assumes no important policy response or local conflict, then later treats both as decisive shocks and limitations.
Attributes death mainly to route difficulty and removes resource shortage and other protection mechanisms.
Sets the risk-tolerance parameter to one for every refugee and provides no heterogeneity or calibration.
Uses 0.5 percent of national population as a hard reception capacity without service or rights evidence.
Omits multiple entry points and intermediate-country capacity, legal, and congestion constraints.
Centrally reallocates refugees among countries and assumes no source return without consent, legal status, family unity, or movement cost.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Cites headline arrivals and deaths but does not reconcile dates, migrant and refugee categories, flows, stocks, deaths, and missing persons.
Provides no source ledger for travel times, death exposures, border delays, route availability, or map construction.
Uses 2013 GDP, cereal, pension, health, and doctor measures without raw values, sources, missingness, scaling, or definition alignment.
Omits the paired country data and uncertainty behind the eleven-country Spearman coefficient.
Prints a source total that does not equal the five source counts and provides no country-node crosswalk.
Says route and destination objectives are standardized but does not print transformations, weights, or units.
Assumes five-percent doctor and twenty-percent food effects without program or evidence data.
Five citations do not cover most route, country, flow, capacity, intervention, and scenario inputs.

models.summary: Combines time and death rate in a transparent expression but fixes one risk preference and lacks empirical calibration.
Uses the first component as living quality without disclosing scaling, loadings, sign, uncertainty, or external construct validity.
Uses a static national population fraction rather than bottlenecked time-dependent service stocks and flows.
Uses Floyd-Warshall on route impedance but omits time-varying borders, intermediate capacities, and path reconstruction.
Combines route and living-quality objectives with undisclosed scaling and a reversed sign for living quality.
Represents unwanted deviations more appropriately but omits numerical goals, normalized deviations, priority values, and a solver-ready record.
Adds arrival-dependent service dilution and reallocation but uses an unsupported coefficient, uniform resource response, and undefined social penalty.
Deletes a border edge and perturbs capacity to explore cascades but supplies no evidence-based shock magnitude or recovery.
Raises demand and exposes infeasibility but changes capacity definitions and provides no overflow or emergency recourse state.

verification.summary: A coefficient of 0.6 with eleven countries lacks data, uncertainty, significance, confounder control, and predictive testing.
Displayed source columns violate the printed source counts, blocking validation of the first allocation.
Displayed row totals and source columns do not match cells or inputs, and the caption names the wrong model.
A more even map is called closer to reality without observed monthly flows, baseline error, or held-out validation.
Uncalibrated percentage changes demonstrate sensitivity only, not intervention effects.
One edge deletion changes a mixed objective whose normalization and orientation are not interpretable.
An arbitrary 30-percent loss has no probability, causal basis, recovery path, alternative magnitude, or compound-shock test.
The tenfold test usefully reveals infeasibility but produces incompatible and negative capacity values and no recourse solution.
Missing raw inputs, transformations, solver, code, and result files prevent independent regeneration.

results_trace.summary: Uses moderate rank correlation to justify capacity-driven prediction without an out-of-sample result.
Claims preference for wealthy countries although the PCA ranks and objective sign contradict that interpretation and the table fails conservation.
Claims route priority moves people toward frontline countries, but the printed result table is internally inconsistent.
Reports a more even pattern and calls it realistic without data, while inheriting objective and parameter defects.
Describes improved resource balance from assumed doctor and food changes but prints no quantified allocation or welfare result.
Reports a 43-percent increase in an opaque objective after removing one connection but does not decompose safety, delay, or overflow.
A 30-percent Belgian decline changes Austria's allocation to zero, demonstrating model sensitivity but not empirical cascade behavior.
Correctly concludes that hard total capacity can make complete settlement impossible, but does not model protected unmet need.
Provides broad actor-specific recommendations without numeric effects, costs, timelines, legal bases, uncertainty, or triggers.

writing_logic.summary: A dense but comprehensive first page lets a judge see mathematical, dynamic, stress, and policy coverage immediately.
The paper explains the abstraction before equations, helping readers connect geography to optimization.
Moves from a weighted sum to goal programming after recognizing conflicting objectives, a sound narrative despite missing implementation details.
Explicitly identifies the flaw in ignoring arrival feedback and adds time and movement among receiving countries.
Organizes policies around route and capacity levers but introduces legal and economic criteria not coherently represented in the model.
Uses a large-demand scenario to expose model failure, creating an honest bridge to limitations even though no recourse model follows.
Names several critical omissions plainly, but summary and recommendation certainty is not fully reduced.
Groups actions by actor and removes equations, producing a readable letter whose evidence trace remains weak.

language_observations.summary: Uses a clear sequence of Firstly through Finally and names models and actions, making broad work highly scannable despite overclaiming accuracy and applicability.
Uses accessibility to name a lower-is-better impedance, creating a persistent direction ambiguity across prose, legends, and objectives.
Calls evenness reasonable and close to reality without a measured comparison and describes countries in imprecise normative terms.
The concise limitations list is unusually candid about overflow, culture, policy, and institutional omissions.
Short actor-based imperatives are usable, but the final moral-pressure sentence is not a substitute for quantified evidence and responsibility design.

visualization_observations.summary: Color-coded routes quickly communicate relative impedance, though edge values, source dates, direction, and uncertainty are missing.
A dual-axis chart makes association visible but omits exact paired data, uncertainty, sample size annotation, and significance.
A small source-transit-destination graph makes the optimization structure easy to understand.
Combines geography and exact allocations, but the table's arithmetic and conservation defects undermine the figure.
Shows the qualitative redistribution after feedback but provides no time series, monthly table, observed comparator, or uncertainty.
Separates route difficulty and receiving capability into a compact hierarchy that improves recap and model navigation.
A standalone page with actor headings and numbered actions effectively changes visual mode for the decision audience.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: C: The summary may have scored well because it exposes a complete multidisciplinary path from data and mathematics to policy, stress testing, limitations, and communication; award status does not prove this caused the result.

C: PCA, shortest paths, network flow, weighted optimization, goal programming, and dynamics provide recognizable mathematical breadth that may have been persuasive in the first year of Problem F despite correctness gaps.
C: Moving from a static allocation to endogenous feedback, interventions, shocks, and scale may have signaled ambition and policy relevance even though the transitions were uncalibrated.
C: Explicitly demonstrating that the model fails when capacity is exhausted may have appeared more credible than forcing an artificial solution and is a genuine practice worth retaining.
C: Route maps, actor-specific recommendations, and a concise letter likely made the work judge-efficient and actionable at a glance; this does not validate the underlying allocation.

weaknesses.summary: Removes family, information, language, law, policy, and conflict mechanisms central to refugee decisions and protection.
Uses one uncalibrated risk preference and incomplete mortality mechanisms and calls a lower-is-better impedance accessibility.
No raw data, scaling, loadings, sign orientation, or outcome validation supports the living-quality label.
Scores rank Hungary and Turkey high and France, Spain, and the UK low while prose asserts wealthy-country attractiveness.
A 0.5-percent population ceiling is arbitrary and does not represent housing, processing, services, law, finance, or geography.
Spearman 0.6 on eleven undisclosed pairs is used as predictive justification without uncertainty or held-out data.
Five source counts sum to 862,527 while the printed total is 14,078.
The weighted model minimizes positive living quality, reversing the stated maximization goal.
Normalization, weights, targets, priorities, and stakeholder basis are absent.
Printed flows violate source conservation, including a tenfold A3 mismatch and a 100,000-unit A4 shortfall.
Displayed row totals and cells disagree and source columns fail to match inputs, making the result unauditable.
The derived 0.5-percent feedback factor is replaced by 1.5 without evidence, changing the effect by a factor of 300.
Cereal, doctors, GDP, pension, and health variables receive one dilution mechanism despite incompatible denominators and dynamics.
Adds f(m) for security and resentment with no formula, unit, data, or causal definition.
Repeated centralized reallocation is called realistic movement without law, consent, family unity, behavior, or validation.
NGO resource changes are arbitrary percentages with no delivery system, cost, coverage, delay, or outcome evidence.
Base, scaling prose, and table imply 0.5-percent, 10-percent, and about 1-percent ceilings, respectively.
Table 7 reports negative capacity values, violating the domain of an allocation upper bound or mislabeling another score.
The model requires all refugees to be settled but has no unmet-demand, queue, emergency shelter, transfer, mortality, or recourse state when total capacity is insufficient.
Recommendations are not quantified, costed, legally grounded, timed, monitored, uncertainty-aware, or linked to exact model outputs.
Five references and no computational bundle cannot support or regenerate the data-rich static, dynamic, shock, and policy workflow.

independent_extensions.title: Rights-constrained agent and household model
independent_extensions.proposal: Represent households, vulnerability, legal status, family and information networks, consent, non-refoulement, asylum processing, and host-community effects as hard constraints and explicit outcomes.

independent_extensions.title: Time-indexed route harm network
independent_extensions.proposal: Use versioned directed edges with time, border, mode, money, congestion, mortality and harm exposure, rescue, and heterogeneous preferences calibrated to observed route shares.

independent_extensions.title: Validated reception-capacity system
independent_extensions.proposal: Model regional housing, processing, health, food, education, finance, and integration as separate stocks and flows with bottlenecks, rights minima, NGO expansion, and uncertainty.

independent_extensions.title: Oriented and validated country indicators
independent_extensions.proposal: Publish standardized PCA inputs, loadings and scores, orient signs, test indicator stability, and validate against reception outcomes; keep normative welfare weights outside PCA.

independent_extensions.title: Invariant-tested robust flow optimization
independent_extensions.proposal: Use rights-constrained multi-commodity time-expanded flow, exact source and node conservation, protected overflow, and automated table regeneration before interpretation.

independent_extensions.title: Pareto and stakeholder decision analysis
independent_extensions.proposal: Orient objectives, publish normalization, elicit stakeholder scenarios, impose hard safety and rights constraints, and show the Pareto frontier, regret, and rank reversals.

independent_extensions.title: Calibrated dynamic service and movement model
independent_extensions.proposal: Track people and legal-service states monthly, estimate service-specific congestion and expansion elasticities, include delays and behavior, and validate held-out trajectories.

independent_extensions.title: Adaptive shock and scale recourse
independent_extensions.proposal: Combine border, capacity, demand, conflict, and disaster scenarios with recovery, compound events, emergency resources, queues, and two-stage adaptive policy under regret.

independent_extensions.title: Policy implementation contract
independent_extensions.proposal: For each recommendation specify actor, authority, resources, budget, schedule, mechanism, capacity or safety effect, distribution, monitoring, triggers, and contingency, then reproduce these quantities in the letter.

independent_extensions.title: End-to-end reproduction bundle
independent_extensions.proposal: Release source ledger, definition crosswalk, raw tables, edge list, node mapping, PCA output, solver model, code, dynamic states, scenarios, invariant tests, and machine-readable maps and tables.

candidate_rule_impacts.rationale: Bound official reconstruction and enforce the confirmed 20-page requirement.
Prevent plausibility, award status, or moral rhetoric from overstating failed or unvalidated results.
Convert broad recommendations into actor, authority, resource, mechanism, outcome, and monitoring contracts.
Keep rights, agency, family unity, legal status, vulnerability, and host impacts inside humanitarian policy models.
Make route harm and accessibility direction, edge data, calibration, and uncertainty auditable.
Require versioned definitions, provenance, exposure denominators, and arithmetic reconciliation for crisis data.
Stop variance compression from being mislabeled living quality without scaling, orientation, and outcome validation.
Replace arbitrary or negative national ceilings with nonnegative service stock-flow capacity.
Make conservation, path, capacity, and overflow invariants release-blocking.
Enforce correct objective directions, preferences, targets, and Pareto robustness.
Require calibrated state timing, service-specific feedback, legal-behavioral transitions, and held-out dynamics.
Turn arbitrary edge and capacity perturbations into evidence-based adaptive resilience analysis.
Preserve definitions and model protected overflow and emergency recourse under crisis scaling.
Distinguish correlations, plausible maps, and sensitivity from independent validation and invariant checks.
Require one reproducible path through data, graph, optimization, dynamics, scenarios, tables, and figures.
Retain the paper's strong map-and-network communication while enforcing exact conserved data and uncertainty.

unresolved_questions: What was the complete official 2016 Problem F wording and which detailed tasks were mandatory rather than paper-implied?
What countries correspond to B1-B11, and what raw route and country data, dates, units, and sources produced every input?
Were PCA inputs standardized, what were the loadings and eigenvalues, and how was the arbitrary component sign oriented?
Was living quality transformed to a cost before the printed minimization, or is the positive sign an implementation error?
What exact normalizations, weights, goal values, deviation priorities, solver, and tolerances generated Models 1 and 2?
Are the inconsistent flow cells transcription errors or actual optimizer outputs, and what are the correct conserved tables?
What system-dynamics estimation supposedly justified replacing 0.5 percent with 1.5, and what is the formula for f(m)?
What monthly observed flows validate the dynamic model and distinguish a planner optimum from actual refugee movement?
Why do the scaling section and table use 0.5-percent, about 1-percent, and stated 10-percent capacity definitions?
What quantity is labeled capacity in Table 7 when several values are negative?
Which strengths actually influenced the judges is unknown; the hypotheses here remain conjecture despite official award confirmation.
